review: Native automatic support locations and cleanup access

manual_readings.reading: Lower and donor/lever-roof sections locate automatic support stock in the open counter-end, common rear passage, donor bay, lever entry and pedestal sockets. No added enclosed cleanup pocket was identified. Fragment stock through these openings and preserve sockets and guide walls.

Current and accepted support overlays occupy the same accessible joint, shared passage, display pocket and dispense region. The current tree layout is different: 48 versus 42 occupancy-linked bodies, with 47 versus 41 lacking interface labels. Those counts are not exact interface or removal-piece counts. No new enclosed support trap was identified. The unchanged joint/display/dispense openings provide fragmentation access; the 4 mm drip hole is not a large cleanup port.
Support topology matches the accepted print (8 bodies); cleanup remains through its open underside before display installation.
Native paths and first/second-layer footprints reviewed; open screw-head recesses supply cleanup access.
Accepted source STL and side-down pose retained; no enclosed removal pocket is introduced.

scope: All native Support-labelled paths, including bodies without interface labels, are considered. Occupancy-linked topology and section-band midpoints locate paths; they do not prove interface count, support release, deposited finish or removal force.
